page: Microsoft Azure D8s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine hypervised via Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance runs on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz, configured with 4 dedicated physical cores supporting hyper-threading to deliver 8 vCPUs. It includes a 480 MB L3 cache alongside 48 KB L1 data and 2 MB L2 caches. Acceleration instructions include AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), covering both amx_tile and amx_int8 instructions for matrix mathematics, alongside cryptographic features such as VAES and SHA-NI.

System memory totals 32.0 GB, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage or hardware GPUs, requiring network-attached Premium Storage disks for persistent workloads. Large-block uncached memory read speeds reach 95.73 GB/sec with write throughput at 40.61 GB/sec, while cached read bandwidth achieves 689.31 GB/sec.

Benchmark results highlight top-tier compression capabilities, yielding 36.55 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 15.22 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression, placing both in the top 10 percent. Multi-threaded decompression delivers 59.13 GB/sec. Across broader tests, the server registers average-tier performance, logging a PassMark CPU score of 16,760.77 and handling 16.48 million Redis SET operations per second. In machine learning inference, small language model text generation achieves 271.19 tokens per second, while 7B model generation produces 10.18 tokens per second.

The absence of integrated local storage presents an architectural tradeoff, shifting persistent disk performance onto remote storage configurations. With balanced compute and memory density, the D8s_v7 delivers steady cost efficiency for enterprise web serving, Redis caching, microservices, and general data transformation pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D8s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine provisioned with 8 vCPUs derived from 4 dedicated physical cores on a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture with a substantial 480 MB L3 cache, the system incorporates AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. It is paired with 32.0 GB of RAM at a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, while containing no bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance testing demonstrates top-tier compression capability, hitting 36.55 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip processing, alongside strong small-model LLM generation speeds. Overall compute, memory bandwidth, and Redis database throughput sit comfortably in the middle tier. The lack of onboard ephemeral storage requires external Premium Storage volumes, making the instance a well-proportioned, cost-efficient resource for containerized microservices, web application hosting, and middle-tier relational databases.
